title: Dualizing objects compose along a closed immersion in the bounded-below etale comparison class
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, and $A=A_{E,n}$ for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module categories on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $h=f,g,gf$, let $Rh_!$ be the compactification-independent etale compact-support functor [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and let $h^	imes$ be its ambient right adjoint. These adjoints preserve bounded-below complexes. The mate of the canonical bounded-below composition $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ is a natural isomorphism
$$ (gf)^	imes|_{D^+}\xrightarrow{\sim}f^	imes g^	imes|_{D^+}. $$
It identifies the composite counit with the pasted counits. For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $a_W:W	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure maps for $W=T,Z$, so $a_Z=a_Ti$. Put $\omega_{W,e}=a_W^	imes A$. Its value at $A$ is the canonical counit-compatible identification $i^	imes\omega_{T,e}\cong\omega_{Z,e}$. Write $
u_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}	o W_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site-comparison morphism. Under $Rh_p^!=
u_X^*h^	imes R
u_{Y,*}$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the site-comparison unit, the same identification on etale-origin bounded-below objects gives $Ri_p^!\omega_{T,p}\cong\omega_{Z,p}$, where $\omega_{W,p}=Ra_{W,p}^!A$.

proof.text: For each $h=f,g,gf$ apply [lem-weil-boundary-etale-adjunction-restriction]. This supplies Noetherian finite-dimensional compactifications and actual adjunctions $F_h\dashv h^\times$ restricting to $D^+$. It also applies to the structure maps used below. Thus every composition and every adjunction in the following steps is in its proved bounded-below domain.

source.place: First proof paragraph: formal dualizing-object composition, re-split assembly step 1.

proof.text:
By [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], the chosen-compactification candidates have the specified choice-independent composition $\alpha:F_gF_f\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gf}$ on $D^+$. Apply [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] to the restricted adjunctions. The resulting $\theta:(gf)^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}f^\times g^\times$ represents the chain $\operatorname{Hom}(K,(gf)^\times L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{gf}K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_gF_fK,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,f^\times g^\times L)$; hence it is the mate of this very $\alpha$, independent of compactification choices. Its pasted-counit identity is
$$\epsilon_{gf,L}\circ\alpha_{(gf)^\times L}=\epsilon_{g,L}\circ F_g(\epsilon_{f,g^\times L})\circ F_gF_f(\theta_L),$$
with source $F_gF_f(gf)^\times L$ and target $L$.

source.place: First proof paragraph: formal dualizing-object composition, re-split assembly step 2.

proof.text: A closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ is proper, hence separated and finite type [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Substitute $f=i$, $g=a_T$, $gf=a_Z$. The constant sheaf $A$ in degree zero lies in $D^+$, so the previous steps give bounded-below $\omega_{W,e}=a_W^\times A$. Evaluate $\theta^{-1}$ at $A$ to obtain $\kappa_e:i^\times\omega_{T,e}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{Z,e}$. Evaluation of the same counit equation proves its normalization; no purity or biduality hypothesis enters.

source.place: First proof paragraph: formal dualizing-object composition, re-split assembly step 3.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-boundary-comparison-composition-transport] to the specified $\alpha,\theta$ of step 2; its compactification and boundedness hypotheses were checked in step 1. For $g=a_T$, its $\lambda_g,\lambda_{gf}$ are $\lambda_T,\lambda_Z$, identifying $S_W\omega_{W,e}$ with $\omega_{W,p}$. Its coefficient-value formula gives exactly
$$Ri_p^!\omega_{T,p}\xrightarrow{Ri_p^!(\lambda_T^{-1})}Ri_p^!S_T\omega_{T,e}\xrightarrow{\rho_{i,\omega_{T,e}}^{-1}}S_Zi^\times\omega_{T,e}\xrightarrow{S_Z\kappa_e}S_Z\omega_{Z,e}\xrightarrow{\lambda_Z}\omega_{Z,p}.$$
The same lemma supplies naturality on all etale-origin $D^+$ inputs and preservation of the pasted-counit normalization.
